[WP] You are the quest giver of the village with a grudge against the hero.

The boy adventurer - they were getting younger with every catastrophe - looked near tears. "Please, sir, I really need the EXP to level before I can beat the monsters in the forest. Can't I do something easier for you?"

I expected to feel the smallest bit of satisfaction from his begging, but all I got was disgust. Who the hell came into a person's house and smashed all their pots, looking for treasure inside, when said person was standing right there waiting for him? When I was a young hero, I knocked on doors before entering, and I asked before looking in trash cans, nevermind antique pots. The kid was scrawny as a starved chocobo, and twice as dumb. He'd probably only taken the easiest tasks so far. Quests were tough in my day, and we did 'em or we died trying. I'd seen a lot of dead adventurers, and the fact that this kid was heir to our legacy was more than a little disturbing.

"That's what I need done. It's that or nothing, son. Maybe you can grind in the last forest for a few years. Uh, I mean levels."

The kid set his mouth and stomped from my house. Good riddance. He wouldn't have lasted a second against the current evil sorcerer dictator anyway.

Three days later, there was a knock on my door. I smiled, glad that I had invested in a lock. Then, the damn thing opened and the kid was standing outside holding a key. Damnit, I left my spare in the neighbor's pot. The kid looked like hell, dirty and bleeding, but I couldn't move out of my spot to help him inside. I wasn't that kind of NPC. He probably hadn't even gone to an inn, the stupid boy. His face was a mixture of pain and triumph, and cradled in his hands was the pot I'd asked for. The one that'd been guarded by a dragon.

I kept my face impassive, staring straight ahead as he limped over slowly. I noticed when he noticed my new pots, painstakingly sought out to look exactly the same as the ones he'd smashed, but he came straight toward me. He was trembling so hard I was afraid he'd drop his prize.

It'd only been three days, but his face was harder, and his muscles larger, his weapons battered, and his coin purse much heavier with gold. He must've done some serious leveling. I was impressed despite myself. I didn't know how to say it, but the weak boy adventurer had been replaced by someone I could respect. Someone who could free us from the sorcerer, given some time.

I opened my mouth to encourage or congratulate him, but all that came out was, "This is a great pot! Thanks!"

The kid - the hero - didn't give much acknowledgement, but stood there expectantly while I granted him EXP and gold. But when I said, "Hey, take this, too!" his eyes widened, and he looked like the little boy from three days ago. I held my old mythril sword out to him, still shining like new with the various spells that'd been placed on it over the years.

He reached for it, almost as if he couldn't believe it was real. I gave him an encouraging smile, and he took the sword. I didn't bother telling him the stories behind it: he would make new ones, and it would serve him just as well as it'd served me. As long as he didn't break my new pots. Because no fucking sword would protect him if he did that.

String Theory is a branch of mathematics.

Arithmetics is a branch of mathematics that studies numbers and operations like addition, multiplication, etc. We assume that numbers behave in a certain way (they can be added, multiplied, etc), and then we can derive cool consequences from that (e.g. that (a+b)(c+d) = ac+ad+bc+bd).

Geometry (planar) is a branch of mathematics that studies figures on a plane. We assume that lines, angles and circles behave in a certain way (see Euclid axioms) and derive cool consequences from that (e.g. the Pythagorean Theorem).

Tensor algebra is a branch of mathematics that studies tensors. Now, while you can easily imagine numbers, lines and figures - tensors are not easily imaginable. They are something like multidimensional tables attached to a space that change together with that space when you shift, twist and turn it. The relations and connections arising between tensors defined in this way are also very interesting.

Now, there is another branch of mathematics, called Quantum Field Theory. It studies even more complicated objects, called "quantum fields". And it so happens, that if we take a very particular and well-defined set of these quantum fields, put them together in the same space and look at them from a very large scale, we'll see large things behaving just like large things do behave in our world!

This configuration of quantum fields is called Standard Model of physics.

Now, String Theory is yet another branch of mathematics studying totally insanely weird objects called "strings" and "branes". Some mathematicians think that if we take a particular configuration of these strings and branes and look at that from a ridiculously large scale, we'll again see large things behaving just like large things do behave in our world!

They couldn't come up with a concrete configuration though, but they have some ideas. E.g. they know for sure that some large classes of configurations do not look like our world at all. They also approximately know which classes of configurations might work, and they are gnawing relentlessly at those, tweaking parameters in hopes of producing our world's physics.

One common thing about all these string theories is that when we smash particles at really high energies (way way higher than what we can do now), they all predict different results than Standard Model does. But we can't smash particles that hard. If we could, we could rule out all string theories at once, or determine that one ultimate Standard String Model configuration that yields real world physics.

So they will have to find another way. Stay tuned.
String theory is in essence an equation that makes sense (has internal logical consistency), and seems to be based on solid assumptions, but we cannot prove or disprove yet.

String theory describes the world as being made up of tiny loops, or strings, of energy that vibrate at different frequencies to manifest different particles. The vibrating energies form the various minute particles, that form the quarks, that form the atoms, that form the molecules, that form everything... Basically.
